intro.TrustedMarkup:
The JSON value tree and its canonical writer.

import { Json, JsonField, emit, emitPretty, jsonEq } from "std/json"
import { parseJson } from "std/jsonread"

This module imports nothing; the reader, std/jsonread, imports it. So a caller that only serializes, such as toJson, links no parser. JNum holds raw number text and objects keep their stored field order, so emit is byte-stable through a parse and generators can depend on the order.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type JsonField = { key: String, value: Json }
type Json = enum { JNull, JBool(Bool), JNum(String), JStr(String), JArr(Array<Json>), JObj(Array<JsonField>) }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A JSON value. JNum holds the raw, validated number text, never a float, so emit -> parse -> emit is byte-stable.
A Json that shares nothing with j; same as j.copy().

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn copyJsonArray(xs: Array<Json>) -> Array<Json>

prose.TrustedMarkup: copy over a list of values; xs.copy() is refused for this element type.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn copyJsonFields(fs: Array<JsonField>) -> Array<JsonField>

prose.TrustedMarkup: copy over a list of object fields, for the same reason.

A copy of the tree with every object's fields in byte order, recursively. Use it for one emission (a diff, content-addressed output); the stored order, which mirrors a Map's insertion order, never moves.

Emit j as compact JSON, field order as stored.

The writers, copyJson and jsonEq recurse at about two frames a level, so a tree nested past about 450 levels traps at the engine's call cap. parseJson refuses input past 128 levels, so only a tree a program builds that deep can reach the cap; bounding it is the program's job.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn emitPretty(j: Json, indent: Int64) -> String

prose.TrustedMarkup: Emit j as indented JSON, indent spaces per level, field order as stored. Empty arrays and objects stay compact ([], {}).

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn jsonEq(a: Json, b: Json) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Deep structural equality, as equality of canonical emits: emit is injective over Json, because kinds have distinct delimiters, field order is kept and numbers keep their raw text.

Writes the encoders toJson calls: for each root, the function that renders its value, and for each node, the function that builds its Json tree. Generated source cannot spell this module's reserved names, so it writes them as VyrnRt_ placeholders the compiler folds back.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type JsonReader = { src: String, n: Int64, pos: Int64, depth: Int64, err: String }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A cursor over one document, which std/jsonread's functions read. It is declared here so that fromJson's generated decoders can name it. depth counts the arrays and objects open at pos; err is the refusal, "" while there is none.
